h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר כ״ה Pesach — Maamar Kaf Hei

p: "דָּא הִיא סְעוּדְתָא דְּחַקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין."
"This is the meal of the Field of Holy Apples."
יִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְשְׁלוּ לְתַפּוּחַ
Israel are compared to an apple tree
(Shabbos 88a),
וּבְמִדְרָשׁ
and in the Midrash
(שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ב', י"א):
(Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:11):
מָה הַתַּפּוּחַ מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁמּוֹצִיא נִיצּוֹ עַד שֶׁגּוֹמֵר פֵּירוֹתָיו חֲמִשִּׁים יוֹם, כָּךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם עַד שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ אֶת הַתּוֹרָה חֲמִשִּׁים יוֹם וְכוּלֵּי.

"Just as the apple tree takes fifty days from the time it puts forth its blossom until it ripens its fruit, so too Israel took fifty days from the time they left Egypt until they received the Torah, etc."
בַּגְּמָרָא הַלָּשׁוֹן: מָה תַּפּוּחַ זֶה פִּרְיוֹ קוֹדֵם לְעָלָיו וְכוּלֵּי, וּבְמִדְרָשׁ הַלָּשׁוֹן: נִיצּוֹ קוֹדֵם לְעָלָיו, כָּךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל הִקְדִּימוּ נַעֲשֶׂה לְנִשְׁמָע

In the Gemara the wording is "Just as this apple tree's fruit precedes its leaves, etc.," while in the Midrash the wording is "its blossom precedes its leaves, so Israel preceded 'we will do' to 'we will hear'"

(מִלְּשׁוֹן הַמִּדְרָשׁ "נִיצּוֹ קוֹדֵם לְעָלָיו" מַשְׁמַע שֶׁתַּפּוּחַ זֶה אֵינוֹ אֶתְרוֹג כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת שַׁבָּת שָׁם דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל פִּרְיוֹ, וְכֵן נִרְאֶה מִתַּרְגּוּם שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב', ג'; אַךְ בַּגְּמָרָא "פִּרְיוֹ קוֹדֵם" זֶה יִתָּכֵן עַל אֶתְרוֹג).

(from the Midrash's phrasing "its blossom precedes its leaves," it is implied that this tapuach is not an esrog as Tosafos wrote in Shabbos ibid., s.v. Piryo, and so it also appears from Targum Shir HaShirim 2:3; however, in the Gemara's wording "its fruit precedes," that could fit an esrog).
וְהָעִנְיָן הוּא: אַף דְּפֶסַח גַּם כֵּן מִסִּטְרָא דְּיוֹבֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
Now the explanation is: although Pesach also derives from the aspect of Jubilee (Binah), as brought in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' מ"ו.):
וַחֲמֻשִׁים עָלוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
"And armed/fifty-fold (chamushim) the Children of Israel went up,"
מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְרָא שַׁבָּת תַּתָּאָה
nevertheless it is called the Lower Shabbos
דְּוַדַּאי בַּלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיָה מִסִּטְרָא דְּיוֹבֵל, וְאִם הָיָה הַתִּיקּוּן כָּרָאוּי הָיָה הַגְּאוּלָה מִסִּטְרָא דְּיוֹבֵל,
for certainly on the first night it was from the aspect of Jubilee, and had the rectification been complete, the redemption would have remained at the level of Jubilee,

אֲבָל כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּסְתַּר הָאוֹר וְהוּצְרְכוּ אַחֲרֵי זֶה לִסְפִירַת הָעוֹמֶר לְהִתְבָּרֵר בְּכָל הַמִּדּוֹת לִהְיוֹת מְזוּקָּק שִׁבְעָתַיִם, שׁוּב נִקְרָא הַפֶּסַח שַׁבָּת תַּתָּאָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יוֹם חֲמִשִּׁים, שָׁבוּעוֹת, מִסִּטְרָא דְּיוֹבֵל, שַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה.

but since the light became concealed and they subsequently required Sefiras HaOmer to be refined across all attributes and purified sevenfold, Pesach is again termed the Lower Shabbos, and afterward the fiftieth day—Shavuos—is from the aspect of Jubilee, the Supernal Shabbos.
וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁמּוֹצִיא נִיצּוֹ—הַיְינוּ תְּחִילַּת הַנָּצַת הָאוֹר, כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהִיא בְּפֶסַח בַּלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה—עַד שֶׁגּוֹמֵר פֵּירוֹתָיו חֲמִשִּׁים יוֹם,

And this is what they meant by "from the time it puts forth its blossom"—meaning the initial budding of the light of Knesses Yisrael, which occurs on the first night of Pesach—"until it ripens its fruit fifty days later,"
שֶׁגְּמַר הַפֵּירוֹת הוּא בְּשָׁבוּעוֹת, זְמַן מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, דִּכְתִיב
for the ripening of the fruit is on Shavuos, the time of the Giving of the Torah, as it is written
(תְּהִלִּים פ"ב, ו'):
(Tehillim 82:6):
אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם,
"I said, you are angelic beings,"
דְּלָא הֲווֹ מַיְיתֵי
so that they would not die
(עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה'.),
(Avodah Zarah 5a),
וְזֶה שֶׁזָּכוּ אָז לְשַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה וְאִתְפְּנֵי יֵצֶר הָרָע מִתַּמָּן
which is when they merited the Supernal Shabbos from which the evil inclination was removed
(תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן מ"ח),
(Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48),
וְהוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע, הוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת
and the evil inclination is the Angel of Death
(בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ט"ז.).
(Bava Basra 16a).
אַךְ אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל: חִבַּלְתֶּם מַעֲשֵׂיכֶם, אָכֵן כְּאָדָם תְּמוּתוּן—עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה גְּמַר הַתִּיקּוּן שֶׁעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִשְׁחוֹט לְיֵצֶר הָרָע

However, after the sin of the Golden Calf—"you have corrupted your deeds, indeed like Adam you shall die"—until the final rectification when the Holy One, blessed is He, will slaughter the evil inclination
(סוּכָּה נ"ב.)
(Sukkah 52a)
וּבִלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח.
and "He will swallow up death forever."
וְעַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת נִגְאָלִין:
And through the observance of Shabbos, Israel are redeemed:
וּבַגְּמָרָא
in the Gemara
(שַׁבָּת קי"ח:):
(Shabbos 118b):
אִלְמָלֵי מְשַׁמְּרִין שְׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת מִיָּד נִגְאָלִין,
"Were Israel to observe two Shabbasos, they would immediately be redeemed,"
וּבִירוּשַׁלְמִי אִיתָא
while in the Yerushalmi it is stated
(תַּעֲנִית פֶּרֶק א' הֲלָכָה א')
(Taanis 1:1)
שֶׁאִילּוּ שָׁמְרוּ שַׁבָּת אַחַת מִיָּד נִגְאָלִין.
that had they observed even a single Shabbos, they would immediately be redeemed.
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ שֶׁעִנְיַן שְׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא
And we have already explained that the concept of "two Shabbasos" is based on what is brought
(תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן מ"ח):
(Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48):
תְּרֵין זִימְנִין אִדְּכַר הָכָא "שַׁבָּת" לָקֳבֵל שְׁכִינְתָּא עִילָּאָה וְתַתָּאָה
"Twice 'Shabbos' is mentioned here, corresponding to the Upper Shechinah and the Lower Shechinah"
וְהַיְינוּ שַׁבָּת תַּתָּאָה, שַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה, וְאָמַר: זַכָּאָה מַאן דְּעָבֵיד לוֹן דִּירָה בִּתְרֵי בָּתֵּי לִיבָּא בְּשַׁבָּת וְאִתְפְּנֵי יֵצֶר הָרָע מִתַּמָּן וְכוּלֵּי.

which are the Lower Shabbos and the Supernal Shabbos, and it states: "Fortunate is he who makes a dwelling for them in the two chambers of the heart on Shabbos so that the evil inclination is removed from there, etc."
וְכֵן נֶחְשַׁב
And likewise it was reckoned
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' צ"ב.)
(Ra'aya Mehemna, Zohar, Vol. 2, 92a)
שָׁלֹשׁ קְדוּשּׁוֹת: שַׁבָּת דְּלֵילְיָא, שַׁבָּת דִּיוֹמָא, שַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה,
three levels of holiness: the Shabbos of night, the Shabbos of day, and the Supernal Shabbos,
וּסְעוּדָה זוֹ דַּחֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין שַׁבָּת דְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא, וּבַבֹּקֶר שַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה.
and this meal of the Field of Apples is the Shabbos of Friday night, while in the morning is the Supernal Shabbos.

אַךְ מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה לְשַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה בְּשַׁבָּת אַחַת, עַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת אַחַת זוֹכִין לְקַדֵּשׁ יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁאַחֲרָיו, וְעַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה זוֹכִין שֶׁשַּׁבָּת הַשְּׁנִיָּה יִהְיֶה מִקְּדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה

However, for one who does not merit the Supernal Shabbos in a single Shabbos, by observing one Shabbos he merits to sanctify the weekdays that follow it, and through the holiness of those weekdays he merits that the second Shabbos attains the holiness of the Supernal Shabbos

וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא: אִלְמָלֵי וְכוּלֵּי שְׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת כְּהִלְכָתָן מִיָּד נִגְאָלִין, רַק הָעוֹלָם נִידּוֹן אַחַר רוּבּוֹ, אֲבָל כָּל נֶפֶשׁ בִּפְרָט הַמְּשַׁמֵּר שַׁבָּת כְּהִלְכָתוֹ מִיָּד נִגְאָל.

and this is what they said in the Gemara, "Were Israel to observe two Shabbasos properly they would immediately be redeemed," only the world as a whole is judged according to its majority, whereas every individual soul who observes Shabbos properly is immediately redeemed.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 88a — "'Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest': Why is Israel likened to an apple tree? To tell you: just as the apple tree's fruit comes before its leaves, so Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear.'" Rashi: its fruit buds before its leaves, unlike other trees.

Azaryah said: Just as from the time the apple tree puts out its bud until it finishes its fruit is fifty days, so from the time Israel left Egypt until they received the Torah was fifty days."

He explains that tapuach is the esrog, for 'the scent of your breath like apples' is rendered in Targum 'like the scent of the esrog.' The esrog stays on the tree from year to year… so its fruit comes before those [new] leaves."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 46a (Beshalach) — "Rabbi Shimon said: Because that Jubilee (Yovel) brought them up out of Egypt, therefore 'And chamushim (armed; read 'fifty') the Children of Israel went up from the land of Egypt'; otherwise they would not have gone up. Therefore they waited fifty days to receive the Torah, and from that place the Torah went forth and was given."

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 5a — "Reish Lakish said: Let us be grateful to our forefathers, for had they not sinned we would not have come into the world, as it says: 'I said, you are godly beings… but like man you shall die.'" The Gemara refines: "as if we had not come into the world" — meaning, "had they not sinned, they would not have died." Rashi: since they would have lived forever, we would count for nothing.

Reish Lakish said: He is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the Angel of Death." Rashi: he goes down and leads people to sin, goes up and angers the King with his accusation, and receives permission to kill the sinner.

When the night comes, it invites with it the Shabbos of the day… and the upper Shabbos is drawn upon it; therefore the night meal is weightier."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Seitzei 2 — “The first Shabbos is in the aspect of ‘and Hashem your God will deliver him into your hand,’ for on Shabbos a person attains awe and knowledge, and through it repentance for the future. Then in the weekdays, to fulfil ‘and she shall weep for her father and her mother a full month,’ to mend the past. Then on the second Shabbos he attains the upper Shabbos, which is Binah, the upper Mother, so that the awe and knowledge enter the depths of the heart, and then he is guarded from the accusation of the evil inclination.” Connection: It reads the two Shabbosos the same way, and adds what each stage does: awe and teshuvah for the future on the first Shabbos, mending the past in the weekdays, and Binah on the second.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Kalonymus Kalman Shapira, Chovas HaTalmidim, Three Essays for Senior Students 3 — “Throughout the week a Jew feels the Shabbos and its holiness. If throughout the week he at least guards himself not to damage and lose all with which he was sanctified on this Shabbos, then he becomes wholly sanctified. Perhaps this is the allusion in ‘Were Israel to keep two Shabbasos according to their laws, they would immediately be redeemed’: if you did not feel in the weekdays holiness from the past Shabbos because it was small, keep another Shabbos properly and more holiness will be added to your weekdays, until you find yourself a treasury of holiness and are redeemed.” Connection: The Piaseczner rebbe reads the two Shabbasos the same way, as one Shabbos carrying its holiness into the weekdays so that the next builds on it; he adds the personal avodah of guarding that holiness through the week.
